resolved.title: 读取数据
resolved.description:
[s0l0!-header][h1]Reading Data[/h1][/s0l0!-header] 

It is quite common for data to come in a file format. One of the most popular formats is the [b]CSV[/b] (comma-separated values).
Pandas supports reading data from a CSV file directly into a DataFrame.

For our examples, we will use a CSV file that contains the COVID-19 infection data in California for the year 2020, called '[b]ca-covid.csv[/b]'.

The [b]read_csv[/b]() function reads the data of a CSV file into a DataFrame:[code format="py" ]df = pd.read_csv("ca-covid.csv")[/code]
We need to provide the file path to the [b]read_csv()[/b] function.
[note]Pandas also supports reading from JSON files, as well as SQL databases. [/note]

Pandas支持从CSV文件中直接读取数据到DataFrame中。

在我们的例子中，将使用一个[ca-covid.csv]('/content/assets/9e2529a85d9a7bf0bd91.csv')文件，其中包含2020年加州的COVID-19新冠肺炎感染数据。

**read_csv**()函数将CSV文件的数据读入到一个DataFrame中：

Once we have the data in a DataFrame, we can start exploring it.
We can get the first rows of the data using the head() function of the DataFrame:[code format="py" codeId="3232"]print(df.head()) [/code]
[img id="4558" width="100%"]
By default it returns the first 5 rows. You can instruct it to return the  number of rows you would like as an argument (for example, [b]df.head(10)[/b] will return the first 10 rows).

We can see that our DataFrame contains the [b]date[/b], [b]state[/b], number of [b]cases[/b] and [b]deaths[/b] for that date.
[note]Similarly, you can get the last rows using the [b]tail()[/b] function.[/note]

content.content:

df = pd.read_csv("/content/assets/9e2529a85d9a7bf0bd91.csv")

[s0l0!-header][h1]Reading Data[/h1][/s0l0!-header] 

The [b]info()[/b] function is used to get essential information about your dataset, such as number of rows, columns, data types, etc:[code format="py" codeId="3233"]df.info() [/code]
[b]Run the code to see the result![/b]

From the result, we can see that our dataset contains 342 rows and 4 columns: date, state, cases, deaths.

We also see that Pandas has added an auto generated index. 
We can set our own index column by using the [b]set_index[/b]() function:[code format="py" codeId="3234"]df.set_index("date", inplace=True)  [/code]The [b]date[/b] column is a good choice for our index, as there is one row for each date.
[note]The [b]inplace=True[/b] argument specifies that the change will be applied to our DataFrame, without the need to assign it to a new DataFrame variable. [/note]

resolved.title: 删除列
resolved.description:
[s0l0!-header][h1]Dropping a Column[/h1][/s0l0!-header] 

Since our data is only for the state of California, we can remove that column from our DataFrame, as it contains the same value for all rows:[code format="py" codeId="3235"]df.drop('state', axis=1, inplace=True) [/code]
[b]drop[/b]() deletes rows and columns.
[b]axis=1[/b] specifies that we want to drop a column.
[b]axis=0[/b] will drop a row.

[note]Now our dataset is much cleaner: we have a [b]date[/b] index, and [b]cases[/b]/[b]deaths[/b] columns.[/note]

你正在处理[ca-covid.csv](/content/assets/9e2529a85d9a7bf0bd91.csv)文件，包含2020年加州的新冠感染数据。
该文件提供了全年的每日病例数和死亡数据。

resolved.problem_statement_en_md:
[s0l0!-header][h1]December 31[/h1][/s0l0!-header] 

You are working with the '[b]ca-covid[/b]' CSV file that contains the COVID-19 infection data in California for the year 2020.
The file provides data on daily cases and deaths for the entire year. 
Find and output the row that corresponds to [b]December 31, 2020[/b]. 
[note]The requested date is the last row in the dataset, so you can use indexing to select it.[/note]
